description: Real-time MCU: ESP32-S3 + onboard QMI8658C 6-axis IMU
notes: Mounted low for acceleration sensitivity. 16 GPIO broken out (1-7, 34-40, 43, 44) vs 14 needed. Native USB - verified, not a UART bridge - so USB MIDI works. 4MB flash, 2MB QUAD PSRAM: confirm quad at E1, octal would eat GPIO33-37. The 8x8 matrix faces out through a tail window as a second display (ADR 0014) - measure idle draw at E1 to size the shared lighting budget

description: Conformal coating for the in-body boards
notes: Breathed into for hours behind 18 unsealed switch cutouts, interior 10-20K above ambient. MASK BOTH SENSOR PORTS FIRST - a sealed reference chamber gains ~5.2kPa when warm and the output clips at zero, looking like a dead sensor (ADR 0003)

description: Passive carrier: dev board headers, ADC, reference, buffers, level shifter, power entry, service header
notes: Must carry the ~22mm cutout under the 8x8 matrix (ADR 0014), the umbilical backing-plate mounting and the service header (ADR 0009). Impossible to add later. The key-scan front end is NOT here - the registers and their 63 passives live on the cluster boards, which takes ~41% of area off a two-layer board that a review costed at ~82% covered with a 22mm hole through it. Nothing on it is fast or RF - 2 layers, hand-assembled

part: 2.54mm female header strip - machined or dual-wipe
description: Sockets for both dev boards on the carrier
notes: Cut to length: 2 strips for the ESP32-S3-Matrix, 2 for the T-Display-S3 AMOLED, 2 spare. SOCKETS not solder-down - a dead dev board is otherwise a strip-down, and was terminal while the body was bonded (ADR 0009)

part: Ribbon, ground per signal - chained cluster to cluster
description: Internal looms: key chain, LED power and data, UART, power
notes: DECIDED 2026-09-21: J-CHAIN is a 2x6 IDC on a 12-way ribbon, alternating ground - GND SCK GND SH/LD GND SER GND QH GND 3V3 spare spare. TWELVE conductors per hop, chained through each cluster board in turn rather than starred. The number of mating connectors is the tracked figure chain-connectors and is deliberately not restated here. It is NOT one per board: SER and QH are point-to-point, so every cluster board but the last carries an IN and an OUT. Every signal has ground on both sides (ADR 0001 item 1, the highest-value SI fix - these four are now the ONLY loom signals that can be corrupted and the blast radius is all 32 bits). Two spares per ADR 0009, free because IDC comes in 2xN. Chain order matters: data must flow TOWARD the clock source, so right_thumb is nearest the MCU and left_hand takes the SER end. This replaces the tail-mounted alternative's 32-44 conductors and ~46 hand-terminated joints

description: Socket for the MPXV4006DP so the sensor is replaceable
notes: ADR 0003 calls the sensor a wear part and buys two. The spare is only reachable if the first part comes out. The body opens on six fasteners now (ADR 0009), so replacing the sensor is a bench job rather than impossible - but it is still behind the lid, which is why it is socketed. Case 1351-01 THT leads on 2.54mm
